results.content: Nearly half of registered voters believe the Supreme Court is biased in favor of President Donald Trump, according to a new Economist/YouGov poll, as Trump has increasingly sought the justices' intervention on election-related matters ahead of the midterms. The poll, conducted September 4-8 among 1,469 registered voters, found that 44 percent said the Supreme Court is biased in favor of Trump, while just 12 percent said it is biased against him. Among Democrats, 77 percent said the Court favors Trump, while 20 percent of Republicans said it is biased against him and nearly 50 percent said it treats him fairly. Right now, Democrats have a wave-sized lead on the generic ballot: about 6 or 7 percentage points, on average. They probably won't reprise 2018 and flip 41 House seats again in November, in part because red-state Republican lawmakers have recently redrawn congressional maps across the South to benefit their party in ways that blue-state Democrats have been unable to keep up with. But they only need to pick up three seats to win back the House.
